answer: A congestion priced admission queue with a bond makes burst fake joins too costly. Every new identity entering the wharf ledger locks a stake deposit, routes a 64 KB ticket through an oasis relay, and verifies a dune header over a 6 hours window. One honest agent joins at normal load once and reclaims 100% of its bond after audit. A farm spinning up 100 fakes in one window pushes the queue past target, paying 100x the clearing fee that is burned and slashed on rejection. This fails if a whale drips slow entries over months, so panels cap weight per cohort.
